speaker: announcer
text: We interrupt this program to bring you a special bulletin. Nonimaginaires, the brain fogs, are eating Old Man on the Mountain. Five pages are going gray in the high country. The cold is real. Something in the timber is not.

speaker: announcer
text: You are on Harlan Wade's hunt. Seven days of food. The pages are torn. Put them back.

speaker: announcer
text: A torn page. Harlan Wade went up alone for elk, with seven days of food.

speaker: announcer
text: A torn page. A small wall tent. He built the fire high when the cold went below zero.

speaker: announcer
text: A torn page. Steep timber, then benches, then parks where the elk should have been.

speaker: announcer
text: A torn page. It had bark for skin, and eyes that shone green. Where it bled, the blood was amber, like sap.

speaker: announcer
text: A torn page. A chorus of bellows rolled down from every ridge. The mountain kept its secrets.

speaker: announcer
text: Steep timber. The snow takes a boot print and keeps it.

speaker: announcer
text: The benches. These tracks are not elk.

speaker: announcer
text: An elk park, and a fire on the knoll. The tent is Harlan's.

speaker: announcer
text: The treeline is watching. The eyes are green.

speaker: announcer
text: Stand by. The Old Man has been taken by the fog. The bark and the green eyes stayed.

speaker: announcer
text: Old Man on the Mountain has its color back. The ridges are quiet. They are only listening.

speaker: announcer
text: The next ridge is already forgetting its own weather.

speaker: harlan
text: Name's Harlan Wade. I came up for elk. Seven days of food. You can walk with me.

speaker: harlan
text: That's the last of the seven days, if I count honest.

speaker: harlan
text: Below zero last night. I built the fire high and the tent held.

speaker: harlan
text: Those are not elk tracks. Too long. And they do not wander.

speaker: harlan
text: Park opens here. Elk should be feeding. They are not.

speaker: harlan
text: Do not shine a light at the treeline. Something shines back.

speaker: harlan
text: Fog-taken. Hit the gray. Leave the animal under it.

speaker: harlan
text: We are being followed. I have felt it since the benches.

speaker: harlan
text: That is him. Bark for skin. The fog is wearing the old man.

speaker: harlan
text: The spruce. Pin that arm.

speaker: harlan
text: The green went out of his eyes. He is free of it.

speaker: harlan
text: Listen. Every ridge. I am walking back to the truck.

speaker: harlan
text: Keeper. Stay on your feet. I am not packing you out.

speaker: harlan
text: A page. The book wants it. So do I.

speaker: harlan
text: Cache. Take what is useful.

speaker: harlan
text: The truck will remember this spot.

speaker: harlan
text: Truck's right there. We are done on this mountain.

speaker: harlan
text: There. The gray let go.

speaker: harlan
text: He is still in there. The fog is what swings.

speaker: harlan
text: Firelight. It burns the fog off them. Use it.
